items.title: GEO MCP: The Best MCP Servers for Generative Engine Optimization
items.content:
A GEO MCP server plugs generative engine optimisation tools straight into your AI agent: ask Claude, Hermes or Cursor whether ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google’s AI Overviews mention your brand, which competitors they name and which sources they cite — or audit your site’s AI readiness. In the video below I show my free GEO system with Hermes Agent. Here are the GEO MCP servers worth knowing and how to use them.

Key takeaways

MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets agents use external tools.
GEO MCP servers do two jobs: AI visibility tracking and site GEO audits.
Options include Cite42, mcp-geo, Naia, Luce, mcp-geo-server and geo-optimizer-mcp.
Pair a GEO MCP with Search Console data and real case studies.






What a GEO MCP is
MCP is a standard way to connect AI agents to tools and data. A GEO MCP server exposes GEO tools — like “check whether ChatGPT mentions my brand for this prompt” or “score this page’s AI readiness” — so your agent can call them during a conversation. Instead of manually testing prompts in five AI engines, you ask your agent and it runs the checks for you.
The best GEO MCP servers




GEO MCP
What it does
Notes




Cite42
Checks whether ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and AI Overviews mention you, which competitors they name and which sources they cite; plus keyword data
Pay per call; works in Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT


mcp-geo
Runs prompts across the major AI engines and stores citations and visibility metrics
Open source (MIT)


Naia
Hosted GEO platform: visibility analysis, content generation, execution plans
API key


Luce
GEO plus SEO audits and Reddit marketing
OAuth sign-in


mcp-geo-server
Technical SEO, AI crawler directives (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) and answer-engine readiness audits
Open source


geo-optimizer-mcp
Scores a site’s AI readiness 0–100 with a grade
Runs locally, no account




These are listings from each project’s own pages; features and pricing change, so check the current docs before you rely on one.

How to use a GEO MCP with Claude or Hermes

Add the MCP server to your agent (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or Hermes all support MCP).
Ask it to test your 10 money prompts across AI engines and summarise who gets mentioned.
Ask it to audit your key pages for AI readiness.
Feed it your Search Console export to find what already works.
Turn the findings into a content plan — then write pages built on real case studies.

I export Search Console data to a CSV, give it to Hermes running a free DeepSeek model, and ask it to analyse what’s working and suggest GEO keywords. It builds a report in the workspace, then my SEO skill writes and publishes pages to WordPress. A GEO MCP adds live AI-visibility checks on top.
What a GEO MCP can’t do
A tool can tell you whether you’re cited — it can’t make you citable. That comes from the three moves behind all my GEO results:




Move
What it means
How I do it




1. Be the source
AI repeats what it reads, so be what it reads
A real case study or experiment in every page


2. Be everywhere
Several sources saying the same thing
Multiple sites, a community and a subreddit, each with its own angle


3. Be first
The first good page on a new topic wins
Publish within 24 hours of a new tool or trend




One rule you can’t skip: on 1 October 2026 Google updated its guidance on AI-generated content to say manual fact-checking before publishing is critical — covering the page text, titles, meta descriptions, structured data and even image alt text — because AI models predict words rather than look up facts. That’s why every page I publish is built on real experience and checked before it goes live.
Results this approach produces

Google’s AI Overview and AI Mode name me first for “best GEO expert” — and cite several of my pages.
The AI Profit Boardroom ranks #1 in Google’s AI for “best AI community”, cited twice.
One site went from zero to 1,300 Google clicks a day, with over 9,600 AI impressions in a single day.
Perplexity lists me several times in its recommendations for GEO experts.

Choosing the right GEO MCP
Pick based on the job. If you want to know whether AI engines mention you and who they name instead, choose a visibility tracker like Cite42 or the open-source mcp-geo. If you want to check whether your site is technically ready for AI — crawler access, structure, schema — choose an audit tool like mcp-geo-server or geo-optimizer-mcp. If you want an all-in-one hosted platform, Naia or Luce may suit you. Start with a free or open-source option to learn what you need before paying for anything.
A simple GEO MCP workflow
Each Monday, ask your agent to run your ten money prompts through the GEO MCP and summarise changes from last week: where you gained or lost mentions, which competitors appeared, which sources were cited. Then pick one page to improve and one new page to publish. That one-hour weekly loop turns GEO from a guessing game into a measurable process.
The bottom line on GEO MCP
A GEO MCP server turns AI-visibility tracking and GEO audits into something your agent does for you. Pick one, plug it into Claude or Hermes, and combine it with real content. Or claim a free strategy session and we’ll show you what’s working.

Yes — Claude Desktop and Claude Code support MCP servers.

Step 1: export your Search Console data
In Google Search Console, export your performance data (queries and pages) to a CSV. This is your most valuable GEO input: it shows what Google already trusts you for.
Step 2: let your agent analyse what’s working
Give the CSV to Hermes and ask: “Analyse this. Based on what’s working, give me keyword and topic ideas that would help us rank in AI search engines.” Mine built a full report: clicks, brand share of clicks, non-brand click-through rate, and what was winning — comparison articles, Agent OS clusters and free AI community pages.

Want us to analyse your Search Console data for you? Claim your free strategy session →

Claim Your Free SEO Strategy Session →

Step 3: pick keywords closest to revenue
From the report, pick topics where you already have impressions, plus fresh topics nobody has covered yet. Comparison pages and “best X” pages are especially strong for GEO because AI engines love to summarise them.
Step 4: write pages around real case studies
This is the step most people skip. Give your agent a real case study — something you tested, a result you got — and have it write the page from your perspective, answer-first, with tables and FAQs. AI engines can generate generic content themselves; they can’t generate your experience. That’s why Google’s AI describes me as known for documenting GEO experiments and public testing.
Step 5: publish with a quality checklist
I give Hermes an SEO skill — about a 100-point checklist — and access to WordPress or Netlify, so it can write, check and publish. But I review before anything goes live.
One rule you can’t skip: on 1 October 2026 Google updated its guidance on AI-generated content to say manual fact-checking before publishing is critical — covering the page text, titles, meta descriptions, structured data and even image alt text — because AI models predict words rather than look up facts. That’s why every page I publish is built on real experience and checked before it goes live.
Step 6: be everywhere and be first




Move
What it means
How I do it




1. Be the source
AI repeats what it reads, so be what it reads
A real case study or experiment in every page


2. Be everywhere
Several sources saying the same thing
Multiple sites, a community and a subreddit, each with its own angle


3. Be first
The first good page on a new topic wins
Publish within 24 hours of a new tool or trend




Step 7: check your AI visibility
Test your money questions in Google AI Mode, ChatGPT and Perplexity every month. I use Perplexity mainly to get a feel for whether we’re being recommended. A GEO MCP can automate the checks.
GEO for local and service businesses
This isn’t just for AI-tool sites. One of my favourite examples is “best HARO agency” — a normal service business — where Google’s AI Overview lists five suppliers and links to us first. The same steps work for a dentist, a plumber or an accountant: answer the questions customers ask, build pages around your real results, get mentioned on local and industry sites, and keep facts current.
Common GEO mistakes on websites
The mistakes I see most: publishing generic AI content with no real experience, burying the answer below a long introduction, relying on one website, covering new topics too late, and never checking whether AI engines actually mention you. Avoid those five and you’re ahead of most of your competitors, because very few businesses are doing GEO properly yet.

Step 1: export your Search Console data

In Google Search Console, export your performance data (queries and pages) to a CSV. This is your most valuable GEO input: it shows what Google already trusts you for.

Step 2: let your agent analyse what’s working

Give the CSV to Hermes and ask: “Analyse this. Based on what’s working, give me keyword and topic ideas that would help us rank in AI search engines.” Mine built a full report: clicks, brand share of clicks, non-brand click-through rate, and what was winning — comparison articles, Agent OS clusters and free AI community pages.

Step 3: pick keywords closest to revenue

From the report, pick topics where you already have impressions, plus fresh topics nobody has covered yet. Comparison pages and “best X” pages are especially strong for GEO because AI engines love to summarise them.

Step 4: write pages around real case studies

This is the step most people skip. Give your agent a real case study — something you tested, a result you got — and have it write the page from your perspective, answer-first, with tables and FAQs. AI engines can generate generic content themselves; they can’t generate your experience. That’s why Google’s AI describes me as known for documenting GEO experiments and public testing.

Step 5: publish with a quality checklist

I give Hermes an SEO skill — about a 100-point checklist — and access to WordPress or Netlify, so it can write, check and publish. But I review before anything goes live.

One rule you can’t skip: on 1 October 2026 Google updated its guidance on AI-generated content to say manual fact-checking before publishing is critical — covering the page text, titles, meta descriptions, structured data and even image alt text — because AI models predict words rather than look up facts. That’s why every page I publish is built on real experience and checked before it goes live.

Step 6: be everywhere and be first

Step 7: check your AI visibility

Test your money questions in Google AI Mode, ChatGPT and Perplexity every month. I use Perplexity mainly to get a feel for whether we’re being recommended. A GEO MCP can automate the checks.

GEO for local and service businesses

This isn’t just for AI-tool sites. One of my favourite examples is “best HARO agency” — a normal service business — where Google’s AI Overview lists five suppliers and links to us first. The same steps work for a dentist, a plumber or an accountant: answer the questions customers ask, build pages around your real results, get mentioned on local and industry sites, and keep facts current.

Common GEO mistakes on websites

The mistakes I see most: publishing generic AI content with no real experience, burying the answer below a long introduction, relying on one website, covering new topics too late, and never checking whether AI engines actually mention you. Avoid those five and you’re ahead of most of your competitors, because very few businesses are doing GEO properly yet.
